title: Biblical Hospitality in the Church
definition: Biblical Hospitality in the Church is the welcoming, generous, and Christlike care shown to believers, strangers, and those in need.
summary: Biblical Hospitality in the Church is the welcoming of believers and strangers into fellowship, care, and shared life.
christFocus: Jesus Christ welcomed sinners and teaches His people to receive others with grace and truth.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Biblical hospitality in the church is the practice of welcoming others with Christlike care. Scripture treats hospitality not as entertainment for friends but as love that makes room for people who might otherwise remain strangers.

This hospitality can include homes, meals, rides, conversations, accessibility, prayer, and simple attention. It is often ordinary, but it becomes powerful when it reflects the welcome believers have received in Christ.

Jesus welcomed sinners, touched the overlooked, and brought outsiders near. The church shows His heart when it receives people with truth, warmth, and wise care.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people can attend church and still feel unseen, especially newcomers, disabled people, singles, grieving families, or those coming out of addiction or church hurt. Hospitality turns doctrine about fellowship into visible love.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look for someone who is present but not yet connected. Invite, include, listen, and make practical room without making people feel like a project. Use your table, time, and attention as tools of Gospel welcome.
